title: A justice review
hook: look back at what you've done for others
tomorrow: Noa says she's done with school forever. so why does Saba laugh?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Jeremiah's letter to the exiles: build, plant, and seek the city's peace. Today closes this stretch on community and justice, with a look back.

End of a season, the coach hands out a sheet: what went well, what didn't, what's next. A theater crew has its own version after the last show, everyone in a circle saying one thing. The Talmud imagines a review like that at the end of a life. Rava says that when a person comes to judgment, they're asked: did you deal honestly in business? That's the first question. Not about prayer. About how you treated people when money was on the table.
screen: `WHAT WENT WELL, WHAT'S NEXT.` → `EVERYONE IN A CIRCLE.` → `FIRST QUESTION: DID YOU DEAL HONESTLY?`

segments.voice: Rava's list goes on: did you set times for study, did you hope, did you search for wisdom. But it opens at the shop counter. And the Torah has a line for this whole stretch: "Justice, justice shalt thou follow." The word twice; some readers hear it as: keep after it, and don't stop at once. Now a neighbor who says something close, in his own words. In the Guru Granth Sahib, the scripture of the Sikhs, Guru Nanak teaches that truth is higher than everything, and higher still is truthful living. Shared ground: in both, what you hold true gets measured by how you live, in the ordinary places where a corner could be cut. And one honest difference. Rava pictures a judgment with a list of questions, and his list moves on to study and hope. Guru Nanak's line isn't a judgment scene at all; it puts truthful living above even truth, as the way a person walks toward God every day. Two traditions, each in its own words, looking hard at the same everyday honesty. Something to tell a friend tonight: in the Talmud, the first question at the end of a life is about business.
screen: `IT OPENS AT THE SHOP COUNTER.` · `JUSTICE, JUSTICE.` · `GURU NANAK: TRUTHFUL LIVING.` · `SHARED GROUND, HONEST DIFFERENCE.` · then, large: `KEEP DOING JUSTICE.`

segments.voice: Choose one way you've shown up for others lately that you'd like to keep going. Name the thing most likely to get in the way of it. Then make your plan in one line: when that happens, I'll do this instead.
screen: `ONE THING TO KEEP GOING.` · `WHAT GETS IN THE WAY.` · `WHEN THAT HAPPENS, I'LL…`

segments.voice: A justice review: an honest look back at what you've done for others, starting with everyday dealings, and a choice about what you'll keep doing.
For today: keep doing justice. The verse says it twice, so once isn't the end. See you soon.

screen: `DAY 1742 COUNTS.` → `COMMUNITY AND JUSTICE · 20 OF 20.` → `TOMORROW: NOA SAYS SHE'S DONE WITH SCHOOL FOREVER. SO WHY DOES SABA LAUGH?`

howItsDone: Jewish tradition sets aside the month of Elul and Yom Kippur for taking stock of one's deeds; the Talmud's list of questions at judgment begins with honesty in business, and Deuteronomy's 'justice, justice' is read as a call to keep pursuing it.
